old_title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal identify Vinicius Jr alternatives as Romero eyes switch
new_title: Transfers LIVE: Liverpool agree Barcola terms, Bouaddi to City close
old_text:
Arsenal have moved on from their chase of Vinicius Jr after he signed a contract extension with Real Madrid and the Gunners have now reignited their interest in Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez, while PSG's Bradley Barcola is also on their list.
Meanwhile, Rodri looks set to leave Manchester City amid interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid. The World Cup winning captain is into the final year of his contract and favours a move to Barca - who are considering a second bid after an initial offer of £38m was rejected.
Liverpool, meanwhile, also want to sign Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and have lined up his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye in what could be a double swoop for Andoni Iraola's side, while the Reds also look to have secured much-needed defender help with ex-Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo set for a loan deal with an option to buy.
Follow all of the latest news, rumours and done deals with our live blog below
Arsenal outgoings - could Zubimendi be on the move?
With Arsenal splashing £75m on Bruno Guimaraes, Mikel Arteta may be required to sanction some sales.
That has led Mundo Deportivo to report that Martin Zubimendi, who only joined Arsenal last year, could leave the club, but only if a potential suitor matches their £77m asking price.
Meanwhile, West Ham are exploring a move for Reiss Nelson who has entered the final year of his contract, as per Sky Sports.
Another Chelsea-Strasbourg loan on the horizon
Filip Jorgensen is set to move to Strasbourg on loan, according to Sky Sports, becoming the latest Chelsea player to make that jump to the Alsace sister club.
Aston Villa in talks for Palhinha - but face competition from Newcastle?
Aston Villa transfer chief Damian Viadagany has confirmed the club are in talks to sign Joao Palhinha from Bayern Munich.
He told Bild: "We are in talks, but there is currently no agreement.
"If something should happen, it is always on the basis of the great respect we feel for FC Bayern.
"We are friendly clubs; our relationship with Max Eberl (Bayern's director of sport), Christoph Freund (Bayern sporting director) and all other responsible persons is excellent.
"Therefore, I cannot and do not want to comment on any further details."
This comes amid reports that Newcastle are also keen on the Portuguese midfielder, who was on loan at Tottenham last term, joining Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg on the list of potential Bruno Guimaraes replacements.
Palace getting busy
As well as potentially signing Dwight McNeil in a swap deal, Crystal Palace are interested in Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and Torino winger Alieu Njie, according to Sky Sports.
Youssef Chermiti stretchered off amid Galatasaray interest
News emerged before Rangers' clash with Hibernian on Sunday that Galatasaray had seen a bid rejected for striker Youssef Chermiti, with the Gers unwilling to sell.
However, the Turkish side's pursuit of Chermiti may now be over after he was stretchered off in that game.
Man Utd working over deal for EFL Apprentice of the Year
Manchester United are working on a deal to sign Leicester City starlet Louis Page, according to BBC Sport.
Page, an 18-year-old midfielder, was named the EFL Apprentice of the Year last term and is an England U20 international.
Hull announce seventh signing of summer
Sweden wing-back Elliot Stroud has joined Hull from Mjallby for an undisclosed fee on a four-year contract.
Shea Charles set for Fulham medical
Southampton midfielder Shea Charles is set to undergo a medical at Fulham after the clubs agreed a deal worth up to £30m, according to the Press Association.
The 22-year-old is expected to sign a five-year contract at Craven Cottage and become the most expensive Northern Irish footballer.
Fulham will pay an initial fee of £26m, while the transfer includes a further £4m in performance-related add-ons.
Ipswich bid for Exequiel Palacios
Ipswich Town have sent in a bid for Exequiel Palacios, according to Fabrizio Romano.
The Argentinian, who is among their key targets, is also being pursued by four other clubs in the Premier League and Bundesliga.
Another big name set for Turkey move
Mohamed Salah's switch to Trabzonspor may have knocked over the first domino of big names making moves to Turkey this summer.
That's because now, Fenerbahce are set to finalise a deal to sign Belgium striker Romelu Lukaku from Napoli, as per Gazzetta dello Sport.
Chelsea will receive a sell-on fee.
new_text:
Liverpool are hoping to swiftly add to the loan signing of Ronald Araujo by hashing out a deal for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola after reaching a reported agreement over personal terms. Barcola leads Liverpool's list of transfer targets and the Reds are in talks with PSG over a fee, though the European champions are demanding £145m to sell the winger.
Arsenal's busy transfer window looks set to continue as they move on from their disappointment in not signing Vinicius Jr. They are hunting alternatives in the forward line with Julian Alvarez and the aforementioned Barcola on their list but defensive reinforcements may yet come in the form of Cristian Romero. The Tottenham captain is rumoured to leave Spurs this summer and is eyeing up a switch to their closest rivals.
Meanwhile, Rodri looks set to leave Manchester City amid interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid. The World Cup winning captain is into the final year of his contract and favours a move to Barca - who are considering a second bid after an initial offer of £38m was rejected. City seem to be making preparations for that outcome as they close in on the signing of World Cup breakout star Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille.
Finally, Manchester United are still searching for a left-back with Newcastle's Lewis Hall seemingly off the table they instead turned their interest on the likes of Antonee Robinson, Jorge Salinas and Joaquin Seys.
Follow all of the latest news, rumours and done deals with our live blog below
Man City close in on Rodri replacement?
Manchester City are closing in on the signing of Ayoubb Bouaddi from Lille, according to the Guardian.
The arrival of Morocco's World Cup breakout star is expected to soften the blow of Rodri's expected exit, with Barcelona increasingly confident of signing the midfielder. Ferran Torres' move to PSG will finance the transfer.
Lille value Bouaddi at £85m.
Micky van de Ven pens new long-term Tottenham deal
Tottenham defender Micky van de Ven has expressed enthusiasm over the club's current trajectory following his decision to sign a new contract.
Reportedly securing a five-year extension, he was delighted to pledge his long-term future to the side, where head coach Roberto De Zerbi views him as a pivotal figure to build his team around.
"It's a special moment to sign a new deal and a proud moment for me and my family," Van de Ven said.
"I've always loved Spurs, from the first day I stepped in here. I love the club, I love the fans and I've developed really well here.
Liverpool agree terms with Bradley Barcola
Liverpool have been given the "green light" from Bradley Barcola on personal terms regarding a potential move from PSG, according to Fabrizio Romano.
It acts as a step forward in Liverpool's pursuit of the Frenchman as the clubs remain in talks over a fee.
However, there is still quite the gap between valuations with PSG wanting £145m.
The problem Liverpool must address after Andoni Iraola's losing Anfield bow draws Arne Slot parallels
When Anfield had last hosted Liverpool, as Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson bade farewell and their teammates embarked on their final lap of honour, Arne Slot had remained sat in the dugout. It proved the last sighting of him in Liverpool. Some 11 weeks later, Slot's successor was a visible presence on the edge of the technical area, Andoni Iraola's constant clapping encouraging his players at the start of a new era. It began with echoes of the old: a 3-2 defeat to Monaco, with a lead lost at Anfield, with a goal conceded to a set-piece, had some similarities with Slot's unravelling, even if the stakes were lower.
Iraola may hope the parallels with last season end when the competitive football starts. As it was, Liverpool outlined why they require Ronald Araujo and how their recruitment is unfinished.
Liverpool given boost in defence as Barcelona star Ronald Araujo joins on loan
The deal gives Liverpool defensive reinforcements and an option to purchase the Uruguay international for a pre-agreed price of £47m.
Liverpool will not pay a loan fee and will cover the centre-back's salary for the length of his time at Anfield, but Araujo's eagerness to join them was such that he took a pay cut.
The 27-year-old, who passed a medical on Merseyside on Monday, is available straight away and will join in team training later this week.
Would Jose Mourinho have worked as Alex Ferguson's replacement?
Jose Mourinho has revealed had agreed to replace Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United and had signed a contract at Old Trafford before deciding to rejoin Chelsea .
The question that hangs over Elliot Anderson and the £100m-midfielder movement

How ageless wonder Virgil van Dijk holds the key to new-look Liverpool's season
Van Dijk has become Liverpool's last centre-back standing but is ready for another long season as he welcomes new teammates and a new manager into the fold.
